autoscaling.description: Autoscaling with CPU or memory utilization percentage </br> Ref: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/run-application/horizontal-pod-autoscale/

gateway.description: Frontend Gateway API configuration (Gateway + HTTPRoute resources) </br> Ref: https://gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io/ </br> Requires Gateway API CRDs installed in the cluster. </br> TLS is configured at the Gateway listener level, not the HTTPRoute.

className.description: GatewayClass name - required when create is true

create.description: Set to true to let the chart create and manage the Gateway resource.

hostnames.description: Hostnames to match (leave empty to match all hostnames)

listeners.description: Gateway listeners - used only when create is true

rules.description: Route rules (backendRefs are auto-generated from frontend service config)

networkPolicy.description: Frontend network policy Leaving ingress/egress empty below while enabled is a permissive (allow-all) policy - uncomment the examples to actually restrict traffic.

Ingestion network policy Ingestion never receives inbound traffic from other pods, so set this to just [Egress] when ingress is left empty below - otherwise the chart's default Ingress+Egress fallback also renders an allow-all ingress rule.

configMaps.description: ConfigMap values to create configuration files Generate ConfigMap with following name: <release-name>-<name> </br> Ref: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/configmap/

volumes.description: Additional volumes on the output connector Deployment definition

dnsPolicy.description: Configure DNS policy Options: ClusterFirst, Default, ClusterFirstWithHostNet, None </br> Ref: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/dns-pod-service/

eck-stack.description: ECK stack subchart deployment </br> Ref: https://github.com/elastic/cloud-on-k8s/blob/main/deploy/eck-stack/values.yaml </br> Recommended for production: 2 cores, 8 GB RAM, 16 GB SSD. Defaults stay small; set resources and persistence yourself.

global.description: Global section contains configuration options that are applied to all services

imagePullSecrets.description: Specifies the secrets to use for pulling images from private registries Leave empty if no secrets are required E.g. imagePullSecrets: - name: myRegistryKeySecretName

imageRegistry.description: Specifies the registry to pull images from. Leave empty for the default registry

image.description: Image registry configuration for the base service

tag.description: Overrides the image tag whose default is the chart appVersion

imagePullSecrets.description: Specifies the secrets to use for pulling images from private registries Leave empty if no secrets are required E.g. imagePullSecrets: - name: myRegistryKeySecretName

ingress.description: Ingress configuration to expose app </br> Ref: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress/

lifecycle.description: Configure lifecycle hooks </br> Ref: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/containers/container-lifecycle-hooks/ </br> Ref: https://learnk8s.io/graceful-shutdown

livenessProbe.description: Configure liveness checker startupProbe already gates liveness until the app is confirmed up, so initialDelaySeconds stays 0. failureThreshold/periodSeconds/timeoutSeconds are relaxed (90s of tolerance) so GC pauses or transient load don't kill a healthy-but-busy pod. </br> Ref: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-liveness-readiness-startup-probes/#define-startup-probes

nameOverride.description: String to partially override opencti.fullname template (will maintain the release name)

networkPolicy.description: NetworkPolicy configuration for the server </br> Ref: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/network-policies/

enabled.description: Enable or disable NetworkPolicy Leaving ingress/egress empty below while enabled is a permissive (allow-all) policy - uncomment the examples to actually restrict traffic.

nodeSelector.description: Node labels for pod assignment </br> Ref: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/assign-pod-node/#nodeselector

opensearch.description: OpenSearch subchart deployment </br> Ref: https://github.com/opensearch-project/helm-charts/blob/main/charts/opensearch/values.yaml </br> Recommended for production: 2 cores, 8 GB RAM, 16 GB SSD. Defaults stay small; set resources and persistence yourself.

podSecurityContext.description: Defines privilege and access control settings for a Pod </br> Ref: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-standards/ </br> Ref: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/security-context/

rabbitmq.description: RabbitMQ subchart deployment </br> Ref: https://github.com/bitnami/charts/blob/main/bitnami/rabbitmq/values.yaml </br> Recommended for production: 1 core, 512 MB RAM, 2 GB disk. Defaults stay small; set resources and persistence yourself.

readinessProbe.description: Configure readinessProbe checker A failed readinessProbe only pulls the pod out of Service rotation, it never restarts the container, so this can stay stricter than liveness. timeoutSeconds is relaxed from 1s (too tight under load, caused flapping). </br> Ref: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-liveness-readiness-startup-probes/#define-startup-probes

retries.description: Number of retries before giving up

redis.description: Dragonfly subchart deployment (alias: Redis) </br> Ref: https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/blob/main/contrib/charts/dragonfly/values.yaml </br> Recommended for production: 1 core, 1 GB RAM, 16 GB SSD. Defaults stay small; set resources and persistence yourself.

replicaCount.description: Number of replicas for the service

resources.description: The resources limits and requested </br> Ref: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/ </br> Defaults follow the OpenCTI Core minimum (2 cores, 8 GB). </br> Ref: https://docs.opencti.io/latest/deployment/overview/

rustfs.description: RustFS subchart deployment (S3-compatible object storage, standalone mode) </br> Ref: https://github.com/rustfs/rustfs/tree/main/helm/rustfs </br> Recommended for production: 1 core, 128 MB RAM, 16 GB SSD. Defaults stay small; set resources and persistence yourself.

startupProbe.description: Configure startupProbe checker initialDelaySeconds is 0: failureThreshold * periodSeconds (300s) already covers slow first-boot init (observed ~90-150s in practice), so there's no reason to blindly wait before the first check on top of that budget. </br> Ref: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-liveness-readiness-startup-probes/#define-startup-probes
